title: Auer passes pole-sitter at Turn 2 and wins at Hockenheim
dek: Lucas Auer won Race 2 at Hockenheim for Winward Mercedes-AMG by 6.388 seconds from Lawson, as two five-second penalties dropped pole-sitter Kelvin van der Linde to tenth and Lawson took the points lead.

chapters.title: A level title fight after Saturday
text: Race 2 on Sunday 3 October 2021 followed a Saturday that had reset the championship. Kelvin van der Linde won Race 1 from pole, his fourth victory of the season and the first since the Nürburgring in August, and wiped out a 15-point deficit to take level with Liam Lawson on 188 points. Marco Wittmann's hopes took a heavy blow when he was hit on the opening lap and had to retire, while Mike Rockenfeller completed the podium from 17th on the grid.

The opening lap of Race 1 had also brought a collision between Arjun Maini and Lucas Auer at the Turn 6 hairpin, which ended Auer's race. Auer, who had won at Assen the weekend before, arrived at Race 2 with a car repaired overnight and with the penultimate round of the season still to settle the title.

chapters.title: Van der Linde snatches pole at the last moment
text: Rockenfeller set the early pace with an unconventional single-run strategy. With the track almost to himself in the middle of the session, he posted 1:37.940 and held provisional pole until the final minutes, when the times fell quickly. Maini was the first to beat him, with 1:37.513 on his first flying lap, and Auer went fractionally quicker to give Mercedes a provisional front row.

Van der Linde had aborted his penultimate lap, but improved to 1:37.392 right at the end and took pole from Auer, whose 1:37.479 was 0.087 seconds slower. It was his fifth pole of the season and three points more, and it put him three ahead of Lawson in the standings again. Maini, who had hit Auer a day earlier, was third and equalled his best qualifying result of the year.

Lawson was fourth on 1:37.657, 0.144 seconds off the Audi's pace, after he had essentially completed a single timed run and had set no representative time in the first ten minutes. Juncadella was fifth on 1:37.746, Albon sixth on 1:37.761, Rockenfeller seventh, Götz eighth on 1:37.986 and Abril ninth, with Wittmann tenth, seven tenths off the top. Lucas di Grassi, in his second qualifying in the DTM, was 19th in the fourth Abt Audi on 1:38.950.

chapters.title: Auer dives inside at the second corner
text: Unlike Saturday, the first lap was completed without incident. Van der Linde was heavily ballasted, with 25 kilograms on his Audi, while Lawson ran without success ballast, and Auer made use of that, diving down the inside at Turn 2 to take the lead. By the end of the first lap he had opened a slight gap.

Behind him van der Linde and Lawson spent the opening laps fighting for second. Lawson passed the Audi into the Turn 7 right-hander, only for van der Linde to retake the place at the next corner. On the following lap they banged wheels on the exit of the hairpin at Turn 6, and under braking for Turn 8 van der Linde hit the back of the Ferrari, unsettled it and passed Lawson at the apex. The stewards gave him a five-second penalty, which left him out of the fight for the podium.

chapters.title: A slow stop and a second penalty
text: The mandatory stops reshuffled the order. Van der Linde's stop was slow, which let Lawson back ahead of him, and because the Audi driver did not serve his first penalty in the pits, a second five-second penalty followed. Götz had the opposite experience: a very strong stop from the HRT crew was the key for the Mercedes driver, who passed van der Linde on his out lap and moved onto the podium places.

Van der Linde was later passed by the Mercedes of Götz, Juncadella and Ellis and was sixth on the road, but the added penalty dropped him further. Wittmann also took a five-second penalty for a pit-stop infringement. During Rockenfeller's mandatory stop an Abt Sportsline mechanic suffered an injury to his hand.

chapters.title: Auer clear by 6.388 seconds
text: Auer led every lap outside the stop cycle and took the flag after 34 laps in 57:33.498, his second win of the season and the seventh of his DTM career. Lawson, who could do nothing about the leader once he was in clear air, crossed the line 6.388 seconds behind, and Götz finished 12.080 behind to keep his own title hopes alive.

Auer's Winward team-mate Philip Ellis took fourth, 12.748 seconds back, passing Juncadella on the final lap. Juncadella was fifth, and Albon, carrying 18 kilograms of ballast, was sixth in the second Ferrari, 15.243 seconds behind. Marvin Dienst, standing in for Maximilian Buhk at Mücke, scored his first DTM points in seventh, ahead of Maini, Abril and van der Linde in tenth. Wittmann was 12th, out of the points for the second race in a row, and di Grassi finished 18th after engine trouble had left him near the back of the grid.

chapters.title: Lawson leads by 14 as Mercedes takes the manufacturers' title
text: Auer said the team had had to work through the night again to repair the car after Saturday's collision, and that the effort had paid off. Lawson said the key had been passing van der Linde early and pulling a gap, but described an intense race in which the Audi ran into the back of his Ferrari once, bending the exhaust and burning a hole in the bodywork. He pointed out that, having no success ballast, it was clear van der Linde would struggle to get past him.

The result swung the championship. Lawson, with second place, took the lead on 206 points, 14 clear of van der Linde on 192, whose tenth place earned a single point. Götz was third on 180, and Wittmann, with 165, theoretically still had a chance of a third title at his home track but was effectively out of contention after finishing outside the points again.

Mercedes-AMG also secured the manufacturers' title at Hockenheim, which Götz said he was glad to share with everyone at the brand for what he called a huge commitment to the series. His HRT team-mate Abril was ninth, and Mercedes cars filled fourth, fifth, seventh, eighth and ninth.

The season finale takes place the following weekend at the Norisring, the 2.3-kilometre street circuit in Nuremberg that hosts the end of a DTM season for the first time. Lawson, who had not raced there, said he would prepare as well as possible, and Götz, whose home event it is, said he would take it on without pressure.

facts.v: Lucas Auer won Race 2 in 57:33.498 over 34 laps, 6.388 seconds clear of Liam Lawson, for his second victory of the 2021 season.

facts.v: Van der Linde was penalised for contact with Lawson and again for not serving the first penalty in the pits, falling from sixth on the road to tenth.
